sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.8914 Of 2011
Order:

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue an order, writ or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of mandamus declaring the inaction of the respondents in paying the compensation amount to the petitioner land as illegal, arbitrary and contrary to law and consequently direct the respondent to pay the compensation to the petitioner land acquired in Proceedings No.B2/53/67- 1, dated 09.01.2007 by Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, Sri Ram Sagar Project, S.S.C.J.C.R.G.L.I.P Tarnaka,
Hyderabad issued by the respondent No.1 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act..."
2. Heard Learned Counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for the respondents.
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the absolute owner of the land to an extent of Ac.9.06 guntas in Sy.No.985 of dry situated in Marripeda Village.

The impugned Notification has been issued for acquiring Ac.41.36  guntas for construction of Sri SK,J Ram Sagar Project of 21 R-DBM 60 canal at Marripeda at Warangal District and the same was published in the local newspaper on 21.01.2007.
The respondent No.1 acquired land from the petitioner to an extent of Ac.1.37  cents out of the total extent of Ac.9.06 guntas.

As per notification, survey was conducted and the survey staff showed that some of the portion in Sy.No.985 belongs to one Sri Lakshminarayana and paid compensation amount to him, but the entire land in Sy.No.985 belongs to the petitioner.
The respondents made wrong payment to third party for an extent for an extent of Ac.0.37  out of the total extent of Ac.1.37  to the petitioner as per the survey record.
The petitioner made representation dated 10.04.2007 to the respondent No.1 requesting to pay compensation amount to the remaining land as per the Notification dated 21.01.2007.
The respondent No.1 issued proceedings in Rc.No.D/691/2007, dated 05.08.2008 to the respondent No.2.

Thereafter, the petitioner made several representations to the respondents,
SK,J but, the respondents did not take any action.
Hence, the petitioner approached this Court and requested to direct the respondents to pay the compensation to the land of the petitioner.

4. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition basing on the counter averments submits that as per the Land Acquisition Records, wrong payment was made to Smt. Vangati Somalaxmi W/o Laxminarayana for an amount of Rs.1,30,000/- for an extent of Ac.1.00 guntas in Sy.No.985 of Marripeda Village.

The same has to be recovered from Smt. Vangati Somalaxmi W/o Vermareddi Puspalatha vs The Special Collector, Land ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100698657/

sentences.text: Laxminarayana
and after recovery of the same, will be paid to the petitioner and requested to dismiss the writ petition.
5. In view of the para No.9 of the counter filed by the respondents, the petitioner cannot wait till the respondents have recovered amounts from the third parties.

As per Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the respondents SK,J have to pay interest on delay payment and the Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is as follows:
"34. Payment of interest: When the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of [nine per centum] per annum from the time of so taking possession until it shall have been so paid or deposited:
[Provided

that if such compensation or any part thereof is not paid or deposited within a period of one year from the date on which possession is taken, interest at the rate of fifteen per centum per annum shall be payable from the date of expiry of the said period of one year on the amount of compensation or part thereof which has not been paid or deposited before the date of such expiry.]"

As per Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the petitioner is entitled to receive interest at the rate of nine (9) per centum per annum for one year from the date of possession taken by the respondents and thereafter, fifteen (15) per centum till the realization.

6. In view of the above findings, this writ petition is allowed by directing the respondents to pay the compensation SK,J to the land of the petitioner to an extent of Ac.1.00 guntas in Sy.No.985 of Marripeda Village and Mandal of Mahabubabad District (erstwhile Warangal District) acquired in award Proceedings No.D/323/2006-1, dated 31.03.2007 with an interest of nine (9) per centum from the date of possession for one year and thereafter, fifteen (15) per centum as per Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, within four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
7. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
_ _ _ _____ JUSTICE K.SARATH Date: 15.02.2024
